I now have a complete picture. Here is the full report.

---

## 1. Mechanism: Server-Sent Events (SSE)

The server uses **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** to push live events to browsers. There are no WebSockets involved.

- **Server endpoint**: `GET /api/v1/sse` (registered at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`, line 27)
- **Content-Type**: `text/event-stream` (set at line 48 of `sse_handler.go`)
- **Heartbeat**: A `: heartbeat\n\n` SSE comment is sent every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive (lines 100-105)
- **Client side**: The browser connects using the Fetch API's streaming reader (not `EventSource`) in `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts` (line 104, `fetchSSEStream` function at line 202). It reconnects with exponential backoff (1s initial, 30s max).

## 2. Hub/Dispatcher Implementation

The hub is implemented in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`:

| Component | File | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `SSEEventType` constants (6 event types) | `sse_hub.go` | 13-21 |
| `SSEEvent` struct | `sse_hub.go` | 24-34 |
| `SSEClient` struct | `sse_hub.go` | 48-52 |
| `SSEHub` struct (the central dispatcher) | `sse_hub.go` | **56-60** |
| `NewSSEHub()` constructor | `sse_hub.go` | 63-66 |
| `Subscribe()` | `sse_hub.go` | 71-86 |
| `Unsubscribe()` | `sse_hub.go` | 89-96 |
| `Close()` (shuts down all clients) | `sse_hub.go` | 99-110 |
| `Broadcast()` (the core fan-out method) | `sse_hub.go` | **115-132** |
| `canReceive()` (visibility-based delivery filter) | `sse_hub.go` | 134-144 |

The `SSEHub` is instantiated inside `NewAPIV1Service` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, line 57, and stored as a field on `APIV1Service` (line 36). It is referenced by the `Server` struct in `/bench/repo/server/server.go`, line 38, where `Close()` is called on shutdown (lines 205-206).

The SSE HTTP handler that streams events to each connected client is at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`, lines 34-110. The route is registered at line 125 of `v1.go` via `RegisterSSERoutes`.

## 3. Handlers That Broadcast Through the Hub

Six event types are broadcast from five call sites across four files:

| Event Type | Handler Method | File | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memo.created` | `CreateMemo` | `memo_service.go` | **163** |
| `memo.updated` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` | `memo_update_helpers.go` | **71** |
| `memo.deleted` | `DeleteMemo` | `memo_service.go` | **585** |
| `memo.comment.created` | `CreateMemoComment` | `memo_service_comments.go` | **126** |
| `reaction.upserted` | `UpsertMemoReaction` | `reaction_service.go` | **106** |
| `reaction.deleted` | `DeleteMemoReaction` | `reaction_service.go` | **161** |

Notable design details:
- `CreateMemo` suppresses the SSE broadcast when called internally from `CreateMemoComment` (via a `suppressSSEKey` context value, lines 24-35 of `memo_service.go`), so that creating a comment emits only the `memo.comment.created` event, not both.
- `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` is a shared helper called by `UpdateMemo` and other update paths; it handles both the webhook dispatch and the SSE broadcast.
- The `Broadcast` method performs **visibility-based filtering** at delivery time: private memo events are only sent to the memo creator and admins (`canReceive` at `sse_hub.go` line 134).
- Helper functions for building SSE events live in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go` (`resolveSSECreatorID` at line 12, `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` at line 24).
